item.title: Blocked Highway Drain / Gully Flooding, 29th August
item.description:
Location: At the corner of Cambridge Road Description of Issue:The roadside gully/drain is completely blocked with impacted silt, mud, and fallen leaves. Rainwater is unable to drain away, resulting in standing water/localised flooding along the carriageway and pedestrian footway. The issue has been present for a number of years and has not been fixed by previous works which have only cleared surface debris. Impact:The standing water poses a hazard to road users and pedestrians forced to step into the road. If left un-cleared, the lack of drainage risks structural damage to the road surface and could lead to property flooding during heavy downpours. Action Required:The gully pot requires a mechanical suck-out (vacuum dredging) and jetting to clear the blocked underground pipework. (Images of the standing water and blocked grate attached).

Nearest road to the pin placed on the map (automatically generated by OpenStreetMap): Marlow Road, Anerley, Greater London
Report on FixMyStreet

item.title: Cambridge Gardens, 29th August
item.description:
Every Saturday, in connection with the London Car Boot Sale held at St Augustine’s School, illegal traders and vendors leave unwanted items and rubbish strewn across the surrounding streets and residential area. This park is meant to be enjoyed by local residents and childern. This has been reported to the Council multiple times, yet the same problem continues week after week. It is unacceptable for local residents and is also an entirely avoidable and repeated drain on Council resources, which are being used to clear up after the same commercial activity every weekend. Please arrange for the area to be cleared as soon as possible. More importantly, serious enforcement action is now needed against those responsible, and the organisers of the car boot sale should be required to put effective measures in place to prevent this from continuing. Residents - and the Council - should not repeatedly have to bear the consequences and cost of rubbish and discarded items generated by this event. Thank you.

Nearest address to the pin placed on the map (from OS Places API): Cambridge Gardens, London
Report on FixMyStreet
